title: Rational-point vanishing tangent criterion for a structure morphism
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $p:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ a locally finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $x:\operatorname{Spec}k\to Z$ satisfy $p\circ x=\mathrm{id}$, and let $w\in Z$ be its image. Then $w$ is closed and the structural map $k\to\kappa(w)$ [def-weil-residue-field] is an isomorphism whose inverse is induced by $x$. Moreover, $p$ is unramified at $w$ [def-weil-unramified-morphism], meaning that it is unramified on some open neighbourhood of $w$, if and only if $T_{Z/k,w}=0$ [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space]. No algebraic closedness of $k$, flatness, or global finite type assumption on $Z$ is required.

source.place: Tags 0B2G (lemma-injective-tangent-spaces-unramified), specialized to the structure morphism over k; schemes.tex Tag 01J9 (lemma-characterize-points), for the section and its residue field.

proof.text: Put $K=\kappa(w)$, and let $r:k\to K$ and $c:K\to k$ be the field maps induced by $p$ and $x$. By the residue-field definition and composition of stalk maps, $p\circ x=\mathrm{id}$ gives $c\circ r=\mathrm{id}_k$ after quotienting the stalk maps by maximal ideals. The unital field map $c$ is injective. For $a\in K$, $c(r(c(a)))=c(a)$, so $r(c(a))=a$. Thus $r$ is an isomorphism with inverse $c$.

source.place: Tag 01J9, lemma-characterize-points and the following residue-field diagram; the section identity on local rings.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-residue-tower-local-geometry] with $C=D=Z$, with $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ equal to $p$, with $e=\mathrm{id}_Z$, and with both chosen points equal to $w$. The morphism $p$ is locally of finite type by hypothesis, and the identity is locally of finite type directly from the affine definition. The two actual residue extensions are the isomorphism $r$ of Step 1 and the identity of $K$, hence have degree one. The cited statement therefore gives that $w$ is closed in $Z$.

source.place: Tag 01TE, lemma-algebraic-residue-field-extension-closed-point-fibre, part (2), with the unique closed point of Spec k.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-rational-tangent-cotangent-duality] to the $k$-morphism $p:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, using the structural residue identification of Step 1. The target local ring is $k$, so its maximal ideal is zero. Consequently the cotangent map is $u:0\to\mathfrak m_w/\mathfrak m_w^2$, the target tangent space is zero, and $\mathrm dp:T_{Z/k,w}\to0$ is its dual. The map $\mathrm dp$ is injective exactly when $T_{Z/k,w}=0$. By [lem-sc-dual-map-injective-iff-surjective], this is equivalent to surjectivity of $u$. Both points are closed (Step 2 and the one-point spectrum), their residue fields are $k$, and $p$ is locally of finite type. Thus [lem-sc-rational-unramified-cotangent-criterion] applies and says precisely that surjectivity of $u$ is equivalent to unramifiedness of $p$ at $w$. This proves the equivalence under exactly the stated hypotheses.

lean.statement: theorem rationalPoint_tangent_unramified (k : Type u) [Field k] (Z : Scheme.{u}) (p : Z ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType p] (x : Spec (.of k) ⟶ Z) (hx : x ≫ p = 𝟙 _) : IsClosed ({x (IsLocalRing.closedPoint k)} : Set Z) ∧ (∃ e : k ≃+* Z.residueField (x (IsLocalRing.closedPoint k)), e.toRingHom = (StructureSheaf.toStalk k (p (x (IsLocalRing.closedPoint k))) ≫ p.stalkMap (x (IsLocalRing.closedPoint k)) ≫ Z.residue (x (IsLocalRing.closedPoint k))).hom ∧ e.symm.toRingHom = (Z.descResidueField (Scheme.stalkClosedPointTo x)).hom) ∧ ((∃ U : Z.Opens, x (IsLocalRing.closedPoint k) ∈ U ∧ IsUnramified (U.ι ≫ p)) ↔ Subsingleton (schemeTangentSpace k Z p (x (IsLocalRing.closedPoint k))))
